exercises.name: Jaw jut
exercises.description: Push the lower jaw forward and hold. Works the muscles under the chin and along the jaw.

steps: Sit or stand tall, looking straight ahead, shoulders relaxed.
Slowly push your lower jaw forward so your lower teeth sit in front of your upper teeth.
Feel the muscles under your chin and along your jaw working.
Hold, breathing normally, then release slowly.
instructions.cue: Gentle forward slide. Do not clench.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not tilt your head back or clench hard. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Push the jaw forward only a little.

exercises.name: Fish face (hollow cheeks)
exercises.description: Suck the cheeks in toward the back teeth and hold, to work the cheek muscles.

steps: Relax your face and close your mouth.
Suck your cheeks in toward your back teeth, like a fish.
Keep the shape without biting the insides of your cheeks.
Hold, then relax your face completely.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not bite your cheeks or hold your breath. Stop if your jaw hurts.
instructions.easier: Suck in gently and hold for a shorter time.

exercises.name: Cheek puff
exercises.description: Fill the cheeks with air, hold briefly and release. Wakes up the cheek and lip muscles.

steps: Take a breath in through your nose.
Close your lips tightly and puff both cheeks out with air.
Hold for a second or two.
Let the air out slowly, then relax.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not let air leak, and do not push so hard that it hurts. Stop if your jaw hurts.
instructions.easier: Puff gently and hold for less time.

exercises.name: Smile cheek lift
exercises.description: A closed-lip smile that lifts the cheeks toward the eyes, to work the cheek muscles.

steps: Close your lips and smile as wide as is comfortable, without showing teeth.
Lift your cheeks up toward your eyes.
Keep your forehead relaxed.
Hold, then release slowly.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not squint hard or wrinkle your forehead. Stop if it hurts.
instructions.easier: Smile a little less wide.

exercises.name: Jaw drop
exercises.description: Slowly open and close the mouth through a comfortable range to loosen and use the jaw muscles.

steps: Sit tall and relax your tongue and face.
Let your jaw drop open slowly, as far as is comfortable.
Pause for a moment.
Close slowly and smoothly.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not force the mouth wide open. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Open only halfway.

exercises.name: Jaw side slide
exercises.description: Slide the lower jaw from side to side with control.

steps: Sit tall with your lips relaxed and teeth slightly apart.
Slowly slide your lower jaw to one side.
Return to the middle with control.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch sides.
breathCues: Slide the jaw to the side
instructions.commonMistake: Do not move your head or force the jaw. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Slide only a little.

exercises.name: Chin lift pucker
exercises.description: A small head tilt with a lip pucker, to work the front of the neck and the lips.

steps: Sit tall and slowly tip your face up a little, only as far as is comfortable.
Close your lips and push them gently upward.
Feel the front of your neck working, without forcing the tilt.
Relax your lips and bring your head back to neutral.
breathCues: Tip up a little and pucker
instructions.commonMistake: Do not tip your head back sharply. Skip it if you feel dizzy or it hurts your neck.
instructions.easier: Keep your head almost level and only pucker your lips.

exercises.name: Neck tightener (platysma pull)
exercises.description: Pull the corners of the mouth down to work the broad muscle of the front neck.

steps: Sit tall with your chin level.
Pull the corners of your mouth down and back, as if grimacing.
Feel the front of your neck tighten.
Hold, then relax completely.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not lift your chin or shrug your shoulders. Stop if your jaw or neck hurts.
instructions.easier: Pull less hard and hold for less time.

exercises.name: Vowel shapes (O and E)
exercises.description: Alternate an exaggerated "ooo" with a wide "eee" to work the lips and cheeks.

steps: Sit tall and relax your face.
Push your lips into a small, tight "ooo" shape.
Then stretch them into a wide "eee" smile.
Keep alternating smoothly, exaggerating each shape.
instructions.cue: Round, then wide, then round again.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not strain your neck or hold your breath. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Make the shapes smaller.

exercises.name: Brow raise
exercises.description: Lift the eyebrows and open the eyes to work the forehead muscle.

steps: Relax your face and look straight ahead.
Raise your eyebrows as high as is comfortable.
Open your eyes a little wider and hold for a second.
Lower them smoothly.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not scrunch your forehead hard or tilt your head back. Stop if it hurts.
instructions.easier: Raise them only a little.

exercises.name: Gentle eye squeeze
exercises.description: Close the eyes softly, then open them, to work the muscles around the eyes.

steps: Look straight ahead with a relaxed face.
Close your eyes gently, as if going to sleep.
Hold for a second without scrunching your forehead.
Open your eyes softly.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not squeeze hard. Stop if it hurts or gives you a headache.
instructions.easier: Close the eyes without any extra squeeze.

exercises.name: Lion face
exercises.description: Open the mouth wide, stick out the tongue and widen the eyes to stretch and use the whole face.

steps: Take a breath in through your nose.
Open your mouth as far as is comfortable, stick your tongue toward your chin and widen your eyes.
Breathe out with a long "haaa" while you hold for a few seconds.
Relax your face and close your mouth.
instructions.breathing: Breathe in through your nose, out through your mouth.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not strain your jaw. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Open less wide.

exercises.name: Mewing (tongue posture)
exercises.description: Rest the whole tongue on the roof of the mouth with the lips closed. A relaxed tongue and jaw posture practice.

steps: Close your lips and let your teeth rest lightly together or just apart.
Rest your whole tongue gently on the roof of your mouth, tip just behind your upper front teeth.
Breathe slowly through your nose and keep your neck long.
Hold, keeping your face and jaw relaxed.
instructions.cue: Tongue up, lips closed, jaw relaxed.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not press hard with your tongue or clench your teeth. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Hold for a shorter time.

exercises.name: Tongue press
exercises.description: Press the whole tongue gently into the roof of the mouth, then release.

steps: Close your lips and rest your teeth slightly apart.
Press your whole tongue gently into the roof of your mouth.
Hold for a second, then ease the pressure.
Keep your jaw and neck relaxed throughout.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not press hard or clench your teeth. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Press more lightly and hold for less time.

exercises.name: Slow chew
exercises.description: A slow, small chewing motion with the lips closed, to practise the jaw muscles.

steps: Sit tall with your lips closed and teeth slightly apart.
Make a small, slow chewing motion, as if chewing a soft bite.
Keep the movement tiny and even on both sides.
Stop and rest if your jaw feels tired.
instructions.cue: Small, slow chews. Do not clench.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not chew hard or grind your teeth. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Make even smaller movements, or fewer reps.

exercises.name: Chin resistance
exercises.description: Open the mouth a little against light pressure from your hand under the chin.

steps: Sit tall and place a fist or palm lightly under your chin.
Try to open your mouth a little against that gentle pressure.
Keep your teeth from clenching and your neck long.
Hold, then relax your jaw completely.
instructions.cue: Light pressure only. Stop if it hurts.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not push hard or clench. Stop if your jaw clicks painfully or hurts.
instructions.easier: Use almost no hand pressure, or hold for less time.

exercises.name: Chin tuck
exercises.description: Glide the head straight back to practise a controlled, neutral neck position.

steps: Sit or stand tall and look straight ahead.
Without tilting your head, glide your chin straight back, as if making a double chin.
Hold for two seconds, feeling the back of your neck lengthen.
Release slowly.
instructions.cue: Straight back, not down. Neck long.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not tilt your head down or up. The movement is straight back. Stop if it hurts your neck.
instructions.easier: Make the movement smaller.

exercises.name: Neck rotation
exercises.description: Slowly turn the head to look left and right through a comfortable range.

steps: Sit or stand tall and look straight ahead.
Slowly turn your head to look over one shoulder, only as far as is comfortable.
Pause, then turn the other way.
Keep your shoulders still and move smoothly.
instructions.breathing: Breathe normally. Do not hold your breath.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not crank the neck or lift the chin. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or locking.
instructions.easier: Turn less far, or hold the end position for one breath.

exercises.name: Neck side stretch
exercises.description: Tip one ear toward the shoulder to stretch the side of the neck.

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Slowly tip your ear toward your shoulder, without lifting the shoulder.
You can rest your hand lightly on your head, without pulling.
Hold, breathing slowly, then return and switch sides.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not pull on your head or lift your shoulder to meet your ear. Stop if you feel tingling in your arm.
instructions.easier: Tip your head less far.

exercises.name: Neck forward stretch
exercises.description: Lower the chin toward the chest to stretch the back of the neck.

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly lower your chin toward your chest.
Rest your hands lightly behind your head, without pulling.
Hold, breathing slowly, then lift your head back up slowly.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not pull hard on your head or round your upper back. Stop if you feel tingling in your arms.
instructions.easier: Lower your chin only a little.

exercises.name: Shoulder blade squeeze
exercises.description: Squeeze the shoulder blades together to strengthen the upper back and counter slouching.

steps: Stand or sit tall with your elbows bent at your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and slightly down.
Hold for two or three seconds.
Release slowly.
instructions.breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze, and in as you release.
breathCues: Breathe out, squeeze the shoulder blades
instructions.commonMistake: Do not shrug your shoulders or arch your lower back.
instructions.easier: Squeeze gently and hold for less time.

exercises.name: Wall angel
exercises.description: Slide the arms up and down a wall while keeping the back flat. Mobilises the shoulders and upper back.

steps: Stand with your back, head and hips against a wall, feet a small step away.
Bend your elbows to 90 degrees with the backs of your hands on the wall.
Slowly slide your arms up overhead, keeping contact with the wall.
Slide back down with control.
instructions.breathing: Breathe in as you slide up, and out as you slide down.
breathCues: Breathe in, slide the arms up
instructions.commonMistake: Do not arch your lower back or let your ribs flare.
instructions.easier: Do not go as high, or let your hands leave the wall.

exercises.name: Standing back extension
exercises.description: A gentle lean backward with the hands on the lower back, to ease stiffness from sitting.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your lower back.
Gently lean back, only as far as is comfortable.
Pause for a second.
Return to standing tall.
instructions.breathing: Breathe out as you lean, and in as you return.
instructions.cue: Small, comfortable lean. Stop if symptoms worsen.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not force the lean. Stop if pain increases or spreads into a leg.
instructions.easier: Lean back only a little, or skip it if it aggravates your back.

exercises.name: Knee to chest
exercises.description: Hug one knee toward the chest while lying down to stretch the lower back and hip.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Bring one knee toward your chest and hold it with both hands.
Keep your head down and your other foot flat.
Hold, breathing slowly, then lower and switch legs.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not pull so hard that your lower back lifts off the floor or it hurts.
instructions.easier: Hold behind your thigh instead of your shin.

exercises.name: Pelvic tilt
exercises.description: Gently flatten the lower back into the floor by tilting the pelvis. A basic spine and core control exercise.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Tighten your tummy and tilt your pelvis so your lower back presses gently into the floor.
Hold for three seconds without holding your breath.
Release back to a relaxed position.
instructions.commonMistake: Do not push with your legs or squeeze your buttocks hard.
instructions.easier: Make the movement smaller.
